rv.q: If I enjoyed it more second time around, it's partly because Wade has grasped a fundamental truth about British life and partly because the play breathes more easily in front of a mixed West End audience.
Now, with Ed Miliband announcing in the House of Commons yesterday that, in spite of a coalition government, the “nasty” party is back, the play gathers further strength.

cn.t: Wade's timely revival of her Oxford dining club satire earns praise for its brutal metaphorical power and grasp of British class dynamics, with critics finding it even more resonant in the current political climate.
